body:
## 2026-11-05-residuals-repoint — the retired residuals file's owner sentences re-pointed to their rows
**Section:** 1. Test Scope Summary · 10. Quality Gates & Coverage Targets
**Change:**
- 5 sentence(s) naming `.andromeda/residuals.md` as where an item is owned or held now name its residual row instead: `res-2iu7qn2e` · `res-6ssktw6x` · `res-ammkrycp` · `res-caouqg3t` · `res-hfvjj77l` · `res-llkgqygv` · `res-tym5wois`.
- Re-point only: what each sentence claims is unchanged (was «a `.andromeda/residuals.md` line»; now «residual `res-…`», which `rec.py get` answers at any status).
**Why:** the records DB's bases door (U61) retired the file, each residual a `residual` row, and re-pointed none of the sentences naming it; the operator's one-time re-point pass (F424), ruled by the overseer, 2026-11-05.
**Ref:** andromedaV3 andromeda-overseer/docs/design-slots/records-db-2026-10-28/f424/ (the pass's manifest)

- State (since 2026-10-10-snapshot-states): the builder reads `aria-selected`, `aria-pressed` and `aria-invalid` by value on every element — a select's option excepted, its `selected` its chosen state (`select::is_chosen`), true or false, with no `aria-selected` read, and its non-empty `label` attribute its `label` where it has no `aria-label` — — trimmed, lower-case, exact — onto the node's `selected`, `toggled` (`mixed` kept) and `invalid` (a value outside the list reads True); `aria-pressed` sets `toggled` on every role but the five checkable ones, and `aria-checked` `true` / `false` / `mixed` sets it on a `CheckBox` · `Switch` · `RadioButton` · `MenuItemCheckBox` · `MenuItemRadio` role alone (`role="switch"` mapping to `Switch`), a native `input` of type `checkbox` or `radio` reading neither — the toggle read per role ratified by the founder (2026-10-18), `accessibility_states`' fourth test its pin; each attribute is read once, and the one other write of `toggled` is a native checkbox's or radio's own checked state on a checkable role — `Toggled::True` or `False` from `checkbox_input_checked()`; under any other role it writes nothing, so `pressed` never begins to read on it, `accessibility_states`' `a_click_and_a_space_move_a_native_control_in_the_tree` its pin, what an assistive technology reads of it not measured. The snapshot takes the three from the tree as `selected` · `pressed` · `invalid`, a boolean model with two limits (a mixed toggle reads not pressed; a grammar or spelling error reads invalid). Ratified by the founder (2026-10-10); what an assistive technology reads is unmeasured, the windowed witness, at an active assistive technology, which this version does not reach, owned by residual `res-llkgqygv` on the founder's F1 (2026-10-14), the headless half — the tree the shell hands the adapter — proven on the stand since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions. Check: `accessibility_states` (6, both layout modes; three rounds in the `stand-repeat` leg, a named `--test` of its list; in the `a11y` leg — the fourth reading `aria-checked`'s three values on a checkable role alone and four unchecked natives reading neither attribute, the fifth `aria-pressed` on a checkable role reading nothing). Since 2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts the builder also holds upstream's six reads, as upstream wrote them: `aria-labelledby` (Names, below), `aria-describedby` (the referenced nodes as `described_by`), `aria-description` (its text into AccessKit's description), `aria-expanded` (a boolean, on every element but a single select, which reads none and writes `expanded` from its list's open state), `aria-disabled` (`true` → `set_disabled`) and `aria-level` (a number, with the tag and role defaults); upstream's own `parse::<bool>` `aria-selected` and unfiltered `aria-label` reads were dropped in the merge, so there is still one read per attribute; the snapshot reads no description and its `enabled` reads the `disabled` attribute, so `aria-disabled` moves no snapshot reading; no stand file states any of the six, and the description and the three new closed values leave only to the platform adapter, which no stand binary builds — what an assistive technology reads of them is not measured (ratified as upstream's behaviour by the founder, 2026-10-17).

- Stand markup (attributes only): the flight booker's date inputs state `aria-invalid`, and the stand states no `aria-pressed` — the flight booker's mode is one `select#flight-type`, whose options state its choice by `selected`; the CRUD list is a `listbox` and its rows `option`s with `aria-selected`. Since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness (the operator's decision) the list `crud-list` takes `tabindex="0"` and an `onkeydown` — the third CRUD Tab stop — and, focused, ArrowDown selects the next visible row (the first when none is selected), ArrowUp the previous, Home the first and End the last, as a row's click does. One gap stands open: the rows are not focusable and the tree's focus is the list, never the option — the builder reads no `aria-activedescendant`, so an assistive technology learns the current row only from its `selected` reading; an `aria-activedescendant` read in the builder, or a roving focus, is SC 4.1.2 work outside the tier-0 target, kept unread on the founder's F2 (2026-10-14) and pinned by `accessibility_active_descendant_unread` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18). The second, the list's empty accessible name, closed at 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions: the list is named `People` by `aria-label`. Cells: `cells-grid`, named `Cells` by `aria_label` with no role, is one Tab stop; the arrows move `current`, clamped, and bring the cell into view; Enter opens the editor on `current`, focused, and the editor's Enter commits and returns focus to the grid; Tab leaving an open editor commits it; `.cells-grid:focus .cell.current` draws a 2px outline in the stand accent; role and cell semantics stay out, owned by residual `res-wvatzhpe`.

- Focus: Tab / Shift+Tab via `focus_next_node` / `focus_prev_node`; focusability recomputed on `tabindex` / `href` / `disabled`; focus resets to body on removal; the tree's focus is the focused node only where it is among the built nodes, else `u64::MAX`, the window, so the tree never names a node it did not build; since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness, in every document (ratified by the founder), a pointer click on a `button` (any type) or an `input` of type `submit`, `reset` or `button` focuses it, then submits the form owner when it is a submit button — a disabled form control still stops the walk first, a disabled ancestor `div` not (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), a click on a `select` focuses it, clearing its typeahead and the document's text selection, and on a single select also opens its list or closes one standing, two clicks on one point opening then closing, each focusing (a disabled select stopped by the walk's gate first, so it neither focuses nor acts; a click on a row of an open list choosing it, a disabled row changing nothing and leaving the list open and a group header choosing nothing; a press outside the list closing it with no event, and a driver `click` on an element under the list refused `covered`; a label's click on a bound single select focusing it and opening nothing; an option of a closed single select, under a group too, is not clicked — a driver `click` on one is refused `covered`; a click on a `multiple` select's row runs `click_select_row`, a disabled select stopping it, otherwise focusing the select and clearing the typeahead and the text selection, a plain click choosing the row alone, Ctrl or Meta flipping it, Shift spanning and a disabled row changing nothing), and a click on any other element (a CRUD row, the list) still clears focus; two pointer clicks on one point within 500 ms and 2 px are a double click, read on the document's clock — on a harness-built document the harness's `VirtualClock`, so two driver `click`s on one point with no `advance` between them are a double click, selecting a word in a text input — while each still focuses its target as one click does (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); `:focus-within` matches the focused element and its ancestors by the `FOCUS_WITHIN` element state, while `:focus-visible` never matches; `:open` matches a `details` or `dialog` carrying `open` by the `OPEN` element state, in every document, flipped when a `details`'s first `summary` toggles it through the mutator — `open_state`'s 4 tests, in both layout modes, read the `open` attribute by presence at construction, move it through a mutator write and removal and a summary's click and Enter, and read `:open` matching. Enter and Space (since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness, in every document, ratified by the founder): a pressed Enter on the focused node that is no disabled form control (`ElementData::is_disabled`; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18 — a `disabled` attribute on a `summary` or an `a` gating neither key, as HTML does) dispatches a Click on a `button`, a `summary`, an `input` of type `submit`, `reset` or `button`, or an `a` with `href`; a released Space (`handle_key_up`) dispatches the same Click on a `button`, a `summary`, or an `input` of type `submit`, `reset`, `button`, `checkbox` or `radio` — a link takes no Space, and a text input and a range input take neither key there; the Click (`Node::synthetic_click_event_data`) runs the app's handlers (a Dioxus `onclick`), then `handle_click`, whose checkbox and radio arms dispatch, after `input`, a `change` with the same value, in every document, a checkbox always and a radio only where it was not checked before the click (`checkable_change_event`), while typing in a text input and a range's key and pointerdown fire `input` and no `change` (`text_range_no_change_event`). Range input (since 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction, in every document, ratified by the founder): focused and with no `disabled` attribute (read by presence), it steps up on ArrowRight/ArrowUp, down on ArrowLeft/ArrowDown, goes to its minimum on Home and its maximum on End, every other key doing nothing — each change marks the changed set and fires one `input`, a move that changes nothing none; a click focuses it without moving its value, and a main-button pointerdown sets the value from the hit's fraction of the content box, clamped to [0, 1]. Select: a focused single-choice `select` (no `multiple`) that is no disabled form control (`ElementData::is_disabled`), its list closed, takes ArrowDown / ArrowUp to the next / previous enabled option and Home / End to the first / last enabled option (with none chosen, ArrowDown reads as Home and ArrowUp as End), and a character pressed with no Ctrl, Alt or Meta as typeahead — the first enabled option whose label starts with the text typed, compared in lower case, the text kept for one select until 1 s of the document's clock passes; Enter, and a Space with no typed text standing, open its list on press, on the chosen option and firing nothing, a released Space doing nothing more, a disabled, inert, hidden or empty select opening nothing, and every other key does nothing; each change marks the changed set and dispatches one `input` then one `change`, a key that changes nothing firing none; an `optgroup`'s options are the select's own in tree order, a disabled group's rows reading as disabled. With the list open — an engine overlay on every document, remote pages included — the engine paints it over the page and focus stays on the select: its keys move the highlight over enabled rows and choose nothing, a pointer over an enabled row moving it too; Enter and Space choose the highlighted row and close, Tab in either direction chooses and closes before focus moves, one `input` then one `change` firing and none for the option already chosen; Escape closes with the value unchanged and no event, as a second click, a press outside and a page scroll do, a wheel outside closing it and then scrolling; a close clears the typed text, and a select made inert, disabled, hidden or removed while open closes its list. A list shows at most `MAX_ROWS` 20 and scrolls by key and by wheel, its thumb painted, taking no hit and not draggable, its rows one height, and it opens and closes with no motion. A focused `multiple` select that is no disabled form control takes ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home and End: alone they choose that row alone, with Shift they span from the anchor (with no cursor yet from the last chosen row), and with Ctrl or Meta they move the current row and change nothing; with a valid `size` a key brings the current row into view through `scroll_into_view`; a Space with no typed text standing flips the current row and with text standing joins it, a character with no Ctrl, Alt or Meta chooses its match alone, its disabled rows are never chosen and Ctrl+A is not modelled; the driver's `type` on any select focuses it with no click, so it fires no DOM focus events on a single select either, closes any list and clears the typeahead, a text opening on a space typing nothing, and the driver's `press` holds no Ctrl, so a non-adjacent `multiple` set cannot be built through the driver, a limit its help states, its fix owned by residual `res-hfvjj77l`.

- Platform: accesskit_xplat adapters (windows, macos, unix, android, null); ActionRequested and AccessibilityDeactivated are unhandled TODOs; the tree is built on InitialTreeRequested and rebuilt on a poll that reported work when the document's changed set, taken by that poll, was non-empty — a focus move, a checked change, a rewritten name, a text control's input, a select's changed choice, a single select's list opening or closing and other mutations mark it, a page scroll or a move that closes a list marking its select through `reconcile_select_list` at the next resolve and a wheel elsewhere through `close_select_list`, while a highlight or a wheel move inside a list marks nothing and a pointer move alone does not — through `Document::accessibility_tree` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07; before 2026-10-07 the poll-time refresh never ran; no windowed witness on the dev host — still owed at the platform adapter, the stand building no adapter, kept so on the founder's F1 (2026-10-14), and owned by residual `res-llkgqygv`, an active assistive technology this version does not reach; since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions both halves are proven headlessly on the stand in both layout modes: on Counter, after a drained changed set, each Tab of the whole `tab_order` and an Enter on `counter-increment` leave `has_changes()` true, and the tree read through `&dyn Document` reads the new focus stop and `counter-value`'s new name). A harness settle neither reads nor drains that changed set, and the set is non-empty on a freshly booted harness document — a check reading the flag as "this step changed something" drains first. Names come from text children, a trimmed-non-empty `aria-label` and `<label>` association (`for`-target, else first nested labelable element — a `button`, an `input` whose `type` is not `hidden`, a `meter`, `output`, `progress`, `select` or `textarea`; a hidden input is named by no label); since 2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts an `aria-labelledby` whose targets hold text outranks both (accname 2B) — its loop runs after the `<label>` → input loop, clears `labelled_by` and pushes the referenced nodes, the `aria-label` staying the fallback when the targets hold none — and that text reaches the snapshot `name`. The seven_guis stand names no `accessibility` feature in its own manifest — dioxus-native-dom's reaches it through escher-driver, so both its binaries compile the accessibility modules — and builds no platform adapter (`accesskit_xplat` and `accesskit_winit` in neither graph), so the stand binary gives no assistive technology a tree; re-read at 2026-10-10-mcp-surface, when escher-driver took `serde_json` as a fourth dependency (one lock line, no package), no platform adapter joins the stand graph.

- **OTel SDK:** observed absent — escher 0.1.0 ships no OTel export (ruled by the founder, 2026-10-06): no OTel crate, egress or `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` credential path; the transport and the credential path stay undecided, held in residual `res-fzitzzw2` for a later version.

- `otel-sdk-install` — not in escher 0.1.0 (the founder, 2026-10-06); a cross-version residual, `res-fzitzzw2`. The driver's command span is built (2026-10-07-driver-command-spans): every call handed to `Session::run` leaves one span — target `escher_driver`, name `command`, INFO, built by hand with `tracing::info_span!` — whose eight fields are each recorded only where they apply: `verb` (the verb table's own word), `cause` (one of the eight names `escher_driver::Cause::name` returns, for a refused call — `unknown-verb` · `malformed` · `not-found` · `stale` · `disabled` · `covered` · `off-screen` · `fonts-unavailable`, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), `settled`, `busy`, `passes` and `added` · `removed` · `changed` (the lengths of the returned diff) — fixed words, bools and counts; `snapshot` and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, an accepted `screenshot` — whole, or by `id` — record `verb` alone, an accepted `lint` and a part read (`Outcome::Part`) record `verb` alone too, an accepted `advance` — accepted on every session (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) — records `verb` and the acting fields like every acting verb (its MCP `tool_call` ending `accepted` and parenting that `command`), and a shot's image, its byte size and its `width` / `height`, a lint's findings or their count, and a part's number or the part count, are never fielded; it writes one line per call only where a sink is installed at `info` or below, and none at the default `warn`; since 2026-10-10-driver-cli the `escher-session` host writes it for every hosted call (3 lines for 3 calls at `trace`), a session-level verb or, since 2026-10-12-self-description, the tool-level `help` handed to `run` records its table word beside `unknown-verb`, and a call refused on the command line or in the client opens no span. Since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface a second span, `tool_call` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10, «Span с tool и ending»): one per MCP `tools/call` request, target `escher_driver`, INFO, opened before its params are read and held until its reply is written, two fields only — `tool` (the table's word) and `ending` (`accepted` · `refused` · `error`) — the parent of the call's `command` span by nesting — the session verbs `start` · `status` · `stop` and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, `help`, answered by the server, leave a `tool_call` with no `command` child, a `help` call ending `accepted` (measured in process by `stand_mcp_tools`), no field added; the `escher-session mcp` role writes it, 5 `tool_call` and 3 `command` lines over one CRUD flow at `info` (9 stderr lines built alone, 11 with the workspace, the `blitz_dom::document` INFO line printing twice since 2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep), and `mcp_log` reads 0 ids, 0 names and 0 typed sentinels at `trace` under both builds; `stand_mcp_tools` records both spans in process with a hand-written recorder (not escher's sink), each test under its own because `tracing`'s callsite interest is process-global. The published statement `docs/capabilities.md` restates both spans (closed-word, bool and count fields, stderr only, no driver line at the default `warn`) and the scrub's limits; its pin `.github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py` reads none of these claims, so a change to the span set or to the scrub's limits is made in that document by hand. blitz_dom::Document` in both layout modes; measured at 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions, with `stand_contrast`, `stand_keyboard` and the shared module, the silence probe reading 0) likewise installs
